the effect of cis/trans isomerisation of the coumaric acid side chain on the stabilisation of the anthocyanins, as well as the colour variance of the pigments.
the influence of the trans-cis isomeric form of coumaric and ferulic acid substituants on colour variance and stabilization in anthocyanin pigments.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trans form of coumaric acids is more stable and more effective as a copigment.
the trans-cis isomers of the coumaric acid moiety are able to stabilise the anthocyanin colour, and that this stabilisation is more effective for the trans isomer than for the cis.
the trans-cis isomers are not able to interact in a similar way as the cis-trans isomers, and therefore they are not able to stabilise the colour of the anthocyanins in the same way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of the two coumaric acid isomers in the anthocyanins of P. integrifolia and T. bridgesii is a consequence of their stabilising influence on the colour of the pigment.
the presence of the two coumaric acid isomers in Petunia and Triteleia pigments is a key factor in their stabilisation and in the colour properties of these pigments.
the cis isomer is more stable, and thus the most abundant in the natural pigment, but it also presents a lower colour intensity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cis form is more stable than the trans one.

the trans-cis isomers of coumaric acids can have an important role in the colour variance of anthocyanin copigmentation, which is a crucial feature for the stability and the colour of anthocyanic pigments.

the cis-trans isomers of the coumaric acids present in the anthocyanins from Petunia and Triteleia are responsible for the observed differences in the kinetic constants and colour properties of the pigments.
